rulings: CF-THE-TITLE-DECIDES. The source row's title states '1st Bowman Auto Refractor /499 PSA 9' — no insert-set name, no 'Bowman's Best', no 'Chrome' variant beyond the standard 1st Bowman Chrome product. That matches the checklist row's own parallel (Refractor, auto, /499) exactly, and is corroborated by the destination pool itself already holding an ebay-user-purchase row (128032791220-10084503020016) titled '2024 Bowman Draft Jac Caglianone 1st Bowman Chrome Auto Refractor /499 PSA 9' at the identical checklist address — the same wording, the same grade, a different sale.

CF-A-WHOLE-SCOPE-WRITE-REFUSES-WITHOUT-ITS-SCOPE / code collisions are not identity. CPA-JC is reused elsewhere (2026 Bowman Chrome's CPA-JC is Johenssy Colome) and B24-JCE is reused elsewhere (2024 Bowman's Best autographs, and 2024 Bowman's own non-auto Sky Blue parallel) — neither collision is evidence against this fold, because the destination is judged by its OWN card_catalog row (checklistcenter-2026-08-29, verified, Jac Caglianone, 2024 Bowman Draft, Refractor, auto, /499), not by the prefix string alone. Measured: no card_catalog row anywhere names B24-JCE as an auto Refractor /499 card — its only /499 entry is the non-auto Sky Blue parallel of the unrelated base 2024 Bowman product — so B24-JCE cannot be this sale's destination under any reading of the title.

R22 (key-spelling / seller-code twins fold onto the checklist key). The source address's own cardNumber field stores the lowercase, non-checklist token 'b24-jce' with no card_catalog row backing it at this exact slug — an unaddressable stub, not a second card. It folds onto the checklist-backed CPA-JC row for the same player, same product, same parallel, same print run.

GRADED FIELDS ARE KEPT AS STORED. gradeCompany PSA / gradeValue 9 are carried unchanged onto the target partition; the engine tiers FMV by gradeCompany/gradeValue on the checklist row, so no grade-shape transform is needed or performed here.
